nodes.label: MDC Propagation Pattern
nodes.rationale: Splitting logging auto-configuration into web-only (ServletMdcAutoConfiguration) and non-web (LoggingAutoConfiguration) avoids NoClassDefFoundError in non-web apps. ConditionalOnClass(Filter.class) prevents eager classloading of MdcFilter's servlet inheritance chain in batch/messaging services like twitter-to-kafka-service.

nodes.label: W3C/B3 Trace Context Propagation over Kafka
nodes.rationale: Both W3C traceparent and B3 (X-B3-TraceId/X-B3-SpanId) headers are injected/extracted to ensure compatibility with Dynatrace OneAgent, Splunk OTel, Grafana Alloy, and any W3C/B3-aware consumer. Downstream consumers correlate logs across producer and consumer boundaries.
nodes.norm_label: w3c/b3 trace context propagation over kafka

nodes.label: KRaft Mode (No Zookeeper)
nodes.rationale: KRaft replaces Zookeeper for Kafka cluster metadata, reducing operational complexity. Each node takes both broker and controller roles, uses CONTROLLER listener on port 9093 for quorum, and PLAINTEXT listener for inter-broker communication.

nodes.label: Buildpacks vs Dockerfile Trade-off
nodes.rationale: Buildpacks offer zero Dockerfile maintenance and automatic best practices but are slow (2-5 min/image) and awkward with multi-module Maven projects. Dockerfile gives full control, fast incremental builds, and works naturally in CI/CD. Dockerfile is recommended for all multi-module, CI/CD, and production scenarios.

nodes.label: Multi-stage Docker Build Pattern
nodes.rationale: Stage 1 uses maven:3.9-eclipse-temurin-25 (~1.2GB) to build the fat jar; only the jar crosses to Stage 2 which uses eclipse-temurin:25-jre-alpine (~90MB). Non-root appuser is created, -XX:+UseContainerSupport and -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75.0 ensure JVM respects container memory limits.

nodes.label: .m2 BuildKit Cache Mount
nodes.rationale: --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.m2 (Option A local dev) persists Maven dependency cache between Docker builds without baking it into the image layer. Requires DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 — without it the flag is silently ignored and Maven redownloads everything.

nodes.label: depends_on with service_healthy Pattern
nodes.rationale: depends_on without condition only waits for container start, not app readiness. condition: service_healthy waits for the healthcheck to pass, ensuring downstream services don't start until dependencies are truly ready. Requires spring-boot-actuator on the classpath.

nodes.label: Common Logging Pattern Initial Scope
nodes.rationale: shared-logging-lib was a skeleton with broken include targets, duplicate packages, and missing Kafka MDC. The fix introduced LoggingMdc, MdcFilter, MdcTaskDecorator, MdcContext, ServiceMdcInitializer, KafkaMdcProducerInterceptor, KafkaMdcRecordInterceptor, LoggingAutoConfiguration, ServletMdcAutoConfiguration, KafkaLoggingAutoConfiguration, and logback-base.xml as a drop-in library requiring no @Import annotations.

nodes.label: Logback FILE Appender Eager Open Bug
nodes.rationale: RollingFileAppender.start() opens the underlying file at construction time, not lazily. Any appender declared outside a springProfile block will try to open its file on every startup. Fix: wrap FILE and ASYNC_FILE in springProfile name='staging,prod,file-logging'. Lesson: always gate IO-touching appenders behind a profile or class-level condition.
nodes.norm_label: logback file appender eager open bug

nodes.label: Spring Cloud Config Retry max>initial Assertion
nodes.rationale: RetryTemplateBuilder.exponentialBackoff() enforces max-interval > initial-interval (strict inequality). Setting equal values throws IllegalArgumentException in EnvironmentPostProcessor phase before any bean is created. Config Client only models exponential backoff; no fixed-interval option without a custom RetryTemplate.
nodes.norm_label: spring cloud config retry max>initial assertion

nodes.label: NoClassDefFoundError jakarta.servlet.Filter Auto-config Bug
nodes.rationale: @ConditionalOnWebApplication on a @Bean method cannot prevent sibling reflection traps. getDeclaredMethods0() resolves ALL method signatures eagerly including return types. Fix: extract servlet beans into a separate auto-config class with class-level @ConditionalOnClass(Filter.class). @ConditionalOnClass uses ASM bytecode scanning — never triggers the JVM classloader.

nodes.label: Kafka createTopics Host/Container Address Mismatch
nodes.rationale: Config-server served localhost:19092 (host addresses) but containers resolved localhost to themselves. Also SPRING_KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS was dead because app uses kafka-config.* prefix (custom @ConfigurationProperties), not spring.kafka.*. Fix: env-var placeholders in config-server-repository YAML with internal docker names as docker-side env vars.

nodes.label: KRaft Cold-start Retry Tuning
nodes.rationale: service_healthy only verifies per-broker liveness, not cluster-level invariants (quorum, ISR, leader election). With replication-factor 3 topic creation requires all brokers to agree. Tuned retry-config max-interval to 30s, max-attempts to 6, giving ~60-90s worst-case before KafkaClientException — enough for KRaft quorum to settle on cold start.

nodes.label: spring.factories vs AutoConfiguration.imports Role Split
nodes.rationale: EnableAutoConfiguration key was deprecated in Boot 2.7 and silently dropped in 3.0 — entries placed there compile but never load. spring.factories still actively used in Boot 4 for FailureAnalyzer, ApplicationListener, ApplicationContextInitializer, EnvironmentPostProcessor, ConfigDataLocationResolver, ConfigDataLoader. AutoConfiguration.imports is the only correct path for auto-config classes in Boot 3+.

nodes.label: ASM Bytecode Scanning for @ConditionalOnClass
nodes.rationale: @ConditionalOnClass evaluates via ASM bytecode scanning — never triggers the JVM classloader. This is the only mechanism that lets auto-config classes reference optional classes safely. @ConditionalOnWebApplication evaluates only after the configuration class has been introspected by reflection, making it unable to protect against sibling reflection traps.
